what_its_for: Lanthanum carbonate is used to lower high phosphate levels in your blood if you have chronic kidney disease (CKD) and are on dialysis. When your kidneys do not work well, phosphate can build up in your body, which can weaken your bones and harm your heart and blood vessels. This medicine works by binding to phosphate from the food you eat in your stomach, so less phosphate gets into your blood.
how_to_take: Take lanthanum carbonate with meals or right after eating — never on an empty stomach. Chew the tablets thoroughly before swallowing. Do not swallow the tablets whole and do not crush them into a powder. Take it with all of your main meals (usually breakfast, lunch, and dinner) unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Take it exactly as prescribed — do not take more or less than directed.
dosing: Your doctor will set your dose based on your phosphate blood levels. A common starting dose is 1,500 mg per day, split between meals (for example, 500 mg with each of three meals). Your doctor may slowly adjust your dose, usually every 2 to 3 weeks, until your phosphate level is under control. The total daily dose is usually between 1,500 mg and 3,000 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose at mealtime, skip that missed dose completely. Do NOT take a double dose at your next meal to make up for the one you missed. Just continue with your regular dosing schedule at your next meal. Missing a dose occasionally is not a serious problem, but try to take it consistently with every meal for best results.
storage: Store lanthanum carbonate tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about medicine take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other medicines within 2 hours before or after taking lanthanum carbonate, as it may reduce how well other medicines are absorbed. This is especially important for antibiotics like quinolones (such as ciprofloxacin), levothyroxine (thyroid medicine), and certain other drugs. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or supplements. Avoid eating high-phosphate foods (such as dairy products, cola drinks, processed foods, nuts, and beans) in large amounts, as your doctor may also want you to follow a low-phosphate diet.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek medical help if you experience: severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or constipation that does not go away; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing; bone pain or muscle weakness; signs that your phosphate levels are too low (such as unusual weakness or numbness). Also contact your doctor if you feel this medicine is not helping or if you have any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: Lanthanum carbonate starts working to bind phosphate from your very first dose at mealtime. However, it may take several weeks of consistent use — and possible dose adjustments by your doctor — before your blood phosphate levels are fully under control. Your doctor will check your phosphate levels through regular blood tests to make sure the medicine is working properly.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and over): This medicine can be used in older adults, but they should be monitored closely by their doctor. Children: Lanthanum carbonate is not recommended for use in children or teenagers under 18 years of age. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of this medicine during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known, so your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits carefully. Kidney disease: This medicine is specifically designed for people on dialysis with kidney disease — your doctor will monitor your condition closely.
